stories.title: I-043 -- shutdown-splash terminal reason not observable
acceptance: [I-043] the shutdown splash cannot observe/render the terminal reason (clean shutdown vs cutoff). Wire the ShutdownSequencer terminal reason to the shutdown splash so it renders honestly; never a fabricated reason. ruff clean
stories.completionNotes:
SHIPPED. All four terminal exits of shutdown-state-poll.js now report WHY, on two sinks: a console line (-> chromium stderr -> `journalctl -u splash-grace.service`, grep `[shutdown-splash] terminal`) and a zero-paint `data-terminal-*` attribute pair on <body>. The report carries the SEQUENCER's own phase+reason (lifted off the last shutdown-state actually read) alongside the splash's local cause -- two different facts, both named, neither substituted for the other. Causes: cancelled | state-missing | black-tail-cap | unrecognized-phase.

READ THIS BEFORE REVIEWING THE AC WORDING. The AC says 'renders honestly'; I did NOT add a visible render, and that is deliberate, not a narrowed scope. I-043's own text forbids it: 'US-525 deliberately did not patch the render side... forcing a paint when the state says the shutdown is over would be a dishonest instrument -- the opposite of the rule the splash exists to serve', and its stated requirement is '`journalctl -u splash-grace.service` ALONE should say which of the four terminal cases fired', with 'prefer the console route'. Spec 6 also requires cancelled/unrecognized to abort with NO fadeout, so painting a reason would contradict the phase contract. The DOM attribute is the 'renders' half done at zero paint cost. If PM/Atlas wants a VISIBLE reason, that is a separate call and reverses an explicit Atlas/US-525 decision.

MECHANISM, NOT JUST DECLARATION -- the part most likely to be reverted by someone who does not know why it is there: chromium DISCARDS web-content console output unless the unit passes `--enable-logging=stderr`, so the JS half ALONE would have been an elaborate no-op on the Pi. Both grace units (x11 + wayland) now carry that flag with the reasoning in their headers. NO `--log-level` is pinned on purpose: chromium logs web-content console messages at INFO regardless of which console method is used, so raising the threshold would filter out the very line the flag exists to surface. `--remote-debugging-port` explicitly NOT adopted alongside it (US-522 -- unauthenticated DevTools on a car-mounted kiosk) and is fenced by a test.

NEW TEST INFRASTRUCTURE: tests/ui/shutdown_probe.js -- the closeout splash had no node probe (the boot splash had splash_probe.js since US-499), which is not a coincidence: its only observable WAS window.close(), identical on all four paths. The probe captures console output byte-for-byte, so the tests assert the string the operator actually greps. runShutdownSplash() added to render_harness.py.

4 MUTATIONS, all reverted BY HAND and confirmed byte-exact via `git diff --numstat` (wayland +14/-0, x11 +15/-1, i.e. pure additions, no mutation residue): (A) bare abort() -> 3 RED incl. the static no-silent-exit fence. (B) drop --enable-logging=stderr from the wayland unit -> 1 RED, and the x11 variant stayed GREEN, which also proves the header COMMENT mentioning the flag does not satisfy the guard (the US-501/US-513 prose trap -- the parser has its own self-test with a positive control). (C) fabricate phase='cancelled' when no state was ever read -> 1 RED on the honest-instrument test. (D) collapse state-missing into cancelled -> 2 RED, headed by test_theFourTerminalCauses_areDistinguishableFromEachOther. (D) is the one that matters: the defect was never 'nothing is logged', it was 'a correct abort and a race are indistinguishable', so a single generic reason string would pass a naive did-it-log test and leave I-043 fully open. Distinctness is the property, so distinctness is what is asserted.

GATE: targeted = tests/ui/test_shutdown_splash_terminal_reason.py (15) + the 4 neighbouring suites that share these artifacts (test_shutdown_splash_render, test_splash_min_visible_floor, pi/splash/test_shutdown_splash_wiring, deploy/test_splash_kit) -- 53 passed, EXIT 0. ruff clean on both touched .py files (`make` is not on PATH on this box, exit 127 reads like a pass -- use `python -m ruff check <file>`). FOR PM: full suite is yours at integration; my diff touches no src/, only the shipped kit + tests.

STILL OWED (Pi-side, not closable on the dev box): the validationCriteria drill. The console->journal leg is the ONE link no headless test can prove -- the probe proves the line is emitted, the unit test proves the flag is set, but only `journalctl -u splash-grace.service` on the Pi proves chromium actually forwards it. Do that on the next clean shutdown BEFORE spending a real AC-loss event on it.

stories.title: I-044 -- kiosk XDG_RUNTIME_DIR %U expands to 0 (root) in the splash/dashboard units
acceptance: [I-044] the kiosk systemd units' XDG_RUNTIME_DIR uses %U which expands to 0 (root) -> /run/user/0 permission errors (dconf/dbus). Set it to the real autologin user's runtime dir (/run/user/<uid>). ruff clean; no /run/user/0 permission errors in the journal

validationCriteria.action: boot the Pi + read the kiosk journal
validationCriteria.outcome: no '/run/user/0 permission denied' dconf/dbus errors; XDG_RUNTIME_DIR points at the real user

stories.goal: As a maintainer, I want the kiosk units to use the real user's runtime dir so dconf/dbus stop erroring.

stories.title: Pi<->server schema/contract PARITY GUARD (A-4) -- standing CI test
acceptance: [Atlas A-4 contract list 2026-08-10] a standing CI test (pattern of scripts/audit_address_mirrors.py) asserting Pi<->server agree on the shared contract -- 6 assertions:
1. ENUM PARITY: data_source AND data_quality value-sets IDENTICAL Pi<->server (set-equality both ways). Source of the A-10 saga (Pi got 'foreign', server didn't)

2. APPLIED-SCHEMA NOT PYTHON-TUPLE (US-459 lesson, LOAD-BEARING): assert the APPLIED schema -- server via the real-MariaDB testcontainer (US-464/470), Pi via the SQLite DDL after ensure-schema runs -- NOT the Python constants. A tuple-only test ships green over a broken DB (the drift this guards)

3. SYNCED-TABLE SHARED-COLUMN PARITY: for every table in sync_log.PK_COLUMN, the sync-payload columns exist on BOTH tiers with compatible types. Tier-LOCAL columns (server source_device/source_id, Pi bookkeeping) exempt -- assert the SYNCED surface only

4. PK-RENAME MAPPING PARITY: every synced table's Pi-PK -> server-id rename (sync client map; e.g. battery_health_log drain_event_id->id) is DECLARED + consistent -- catches a new synced table added without its mapping

5. Pi ENSURE-SCHEMA COVERAGE (not a schema_migrations table): every shared/synced column the server declares has a corresponding Pi ensureXSchema helper/DDL column. Pi's ensureXSchema IS its migration equivalent; guard it stays in sync with the server's shared surface
6. TIMESTAMP/FORMAT PARITY: synced timestamp columns use canonical ISO-8601 UTC on both tiers (TD-027/US-202); the sync does no coercion beyond the PK rename, so a format divergence corrupts silently

DoD: name sync_log.PK_COLUMN as the table set (complete-by-construction -- a future synced table auto-covered); run assertion #2 against the US-470 testcontainer + the Pi SQLite DDL. This GUARDS (F-076 normalizes; this keeps it normalized). ruff clean

validationCriteria.action: introduce a deliberate Pi/server shared-contract mismatch
validationCriteria.outcome: the parity CI test fails before deploy

stories.goal: As a maintainer, I want CI to fail when Pi(obd.db) and server(obd2db) drift on shared contracts, so the recurring A-4 divergence is caught before deploy.

stories.title: OBD BT bond self-heal + boot verify (A-18 follow-on)
acceptance: [Atlas addition A-18] on boot / on repeated connect-fail, detect a lost-or-de-bonded state (bonded=no) and auto-run the re-pair path (or loudly surface it) -- never silent capture-death. Include the BT-stack-wedge reset (power off/on + longer scan) that was needed 2026-08-07. verify_bt_pair.sh exists -- wire it into the reconnect path.

[Atlas refinement -- serialize re-pair vs the port] auto-re-pair MUST stop/hold eclipse-obd's connection first (systemctl stop eclipse-obd before pairing) -- never pair while the logger contends on the port ('multiple access' hazard from 2026-08-07)
[Atlas refinement -- bounded, not a loop] cap auto-re-pair (once per boot / backoff) -- never re-pair on EVERY connect-fail (hammers the radio)

[Atlas refinement -- loud-surface when not discoverable] unattended auto-re-pair only works if the dongle is discoverable+unbonded; if discovery does not find it, do NOT silently retry -- surface it (state/log) so the operator power-cycles the dongle (honest-instrument)

validationCriteria.action: clear the bond on the Pi, then boot / attempt capture
validationCriteria.outcome: the Pi detects bonded=no and auto-re-pairs (or loudly surfaces it); capture recovers rather than silently dying

stories.goal: As the operator, I want the Pi to detect + auto-recover a lost BT bond instead of silently dying on capture, so the month-long bond outage cannot recur unnoticed.
